Project analysis based on the defined success metrics.

* *at least 2 Identified growth needs ✅*
1) Lack of time that could be devoted to Learning
_The TLs have a lot of tasks so it is hard for them to devote some time to learn something extra. It would be nice to have a unified approach to the learning time for TLs_ 
2) Unclarity about the learning budget
_Not everyone knew about the learning budget (10 euros per month for everyone in CS). As the result, a confluence page “Self Development Budget” was created where we tried to attend to all the questions related to this budget. 171 people checked this page and there are 363 reviews._
_Additionally, a page with the Suggested Online Courses was created. With the information on what to use the learning budget for. It includes the courses based on the skills that TLs  and the agents were interested to learn and skills that were outlined in the Path to Senior Guide. The page was viewed by 85 people and has 244 reviews._ 
3) What is needed to grow into the Senior Role
_The guidelines “Path to Senior” were created by Refilwe._ 
* *Improvement of the Peakon survey score by 0.4 in comparison with the one coming in February 8.6 ->9.0 🔻*
 _Peakon Survey  Growth Score in May was_ *_8.3,_* _which is lower, than the score we had before the sessions._ 
_It is a general score. There are also specifications: Growth Mentoring 9.0,  Growth Career path 7.8, Growth Learning 8.0. There is a chance that the listening sessions dragged the attention to the fact that there is not so much time and learning opportunities within the regular working time._ 
* *Feedback from TLs on the materials provided (Google Forms Survey)*❌
_Since most of the “materials” are the confluence pages, we can monitor the number of people who got interested in the subject, the Team Leads were leaving the comments and suggestions on the pages themselves._ 
* *20+ team leads participating in the session* 🔻
_18 Team Leads participated in the session (21 registered)_
_There were less TLs, participating in the sessions than we were hoping for. However, the sessions were very engaging and the Team Leads were actively sharing their feedback._ 

*Overall results:*
The sessions really helped to figure out the learning needs/wishes of the Team Leads and as the result, we developed more info pages and a guide that could be used as the helpers. However, only 26% of all the Team Leads were interested in participating in the sessions, which is quite a low engagement. 
Considering the upcoming changes in Q3 and Q4 and unclarity on the future CS situation, it makes less sense to have an additional session in the second half of the year, so we can wrap up the sessions by the end of 2022.

Me and [~accountid:6149a0e9ba1b34006ab04897] had a call with the external counsel today, and unfortunately limiting the scope of liability as the Customer requests (including with “direct” damages) does not provide us comfort. _Unlike in some other jurisdictions (e.g EE), what are “direct” damages is not clarified in the PT statutory law. Nor does the PT case law provide an answer for our (theoretical) concerns, i.e “User missing the million-dollar appointment” or “fines to Customer by the tax office” originally caused by Bolt’s buggy system/setup._

From there I look there are two options (dropping the prospect not being one of them for now):

* we revert to the Customer once more claiming that we can’t accept their wording w/o either (a) introducing at least some sort of monetary cap, or (b) adding an exclusion in these lines: _“Unless intentional, Bolt shall not in any circumstance be liable to the Customer nor User whether in tort, contract, or otherwise for: (i) any failure of its systems that results in the failure or inability to provide Bolt Services or Bolt Business; (ii) loss of profits; (iii) loss of business; or (v) any pure economic, special, indirect, or consequential loss, costs, damages, charges or expenses.”_ I’d argue on common sense based on the example why it’s ridiculous that we should be liable for them missing a “million-dollar” appointment just for requesting a Bolt ride too late to find an alternative. Or play hardball based on the assumption that Uber didn’t meet their needs as well. Or,
* We get this to a decision up to Nick and Finance in terms of accepting the exposure from removing the financial cap. I trust all agree that the cases we’re discussing here are highly theoretical. Until they materialize. And life can be surprising in unexpected ways.

Happy to think along in order to find further alternatives though it seems we are exhausting these.

Comment from local labour lawyer: 
Yes, there is a nuance here.

 

The issue is not if you can insource from Adecco or not, but if you may hire temporary workers. The main rule now - (I’ll come back to proposed changes) – is that if you legally can employ somebody temporarily, you can also insource from an agency like Adecco.

 

The feed  back you received from your in house legal staff is correct, as far as Norway has strict rules related to temporary hiring of personnel. I have also written something similar to you previously.  The main requirement is that you can only employ somebody temporarily when the work i+s of a temporary nature.+

 

The answer you received in yellow below points out to the fact that you cannot employ temporarily for work that will continue beyond the end of the hire period. This is correct, since such work is not of a temporary nature.

 

It is still my view that you may temporarily employ people for seasonal scooter work, (and not just agricultural work). Thousands of people work as waiters during the summer period in outdoor restaurants, and this is of course work of a temporary nature.  This means that you in my view can insource temporary workers for scooter related work that is of a temporary nature. The temporary nature of the work however needs to be correct and possible to prove.   I however agree that you cannot insource people if the only reason is that you can’t find people to employ permanently.

 

So to the proposed changes. The Government has proposed to exclude the possibility to insource people from agencies when the purpose is to fill a temporary position. Meaning, the employer can still hire temporarily for temporary jobs, but they cannot insource people to such positions. There is a lot of opposition to this  proposal, but I expect that it will be passed in 2023.

It is true we are limited in our leverage for fixing delivery slots for suppliers with revenue several times higher than ours and forcing them to stick to tight slots is not working well, but we have some flex with setting delivery days which are fixed more around store capacity than customer requirement. Also we are hoping to roll out central distribution model in few markets in Q3/Q4 - then we’d definitely need this data to optimise store replenishment. 

* Intra-day is not a bad suggestion, it will help us optimise delivery schedule for suppliers who are delivering to us few times per week but not daily.  That would include suppliers that provide us products with long or medium long shelf life, such as your dry staples, meat, cheeses etc
* Hourly is going to help us more with fresh assortment with very short life - fruits and vegetables, dairy, bakery etc delivered daily in markets that have high volumes and here once again once we understand which products are running out at specific hours, we will either adjust delivery schedules or increase frequency or increase stocks as last option (high waste risk) 

Hence there is tremendous value on having this hourly / daily granularity, which we didn’t raise before given the challenges with current non-weighted availability calculation. Especially our primary focus is to improve availability for Anchor & Fresh assortment. [~accountid:622852fd6a4c4c0070b16e6d]  I shared with you lost sales sample calculation. Agree, it gives the weighted element in availability - however some of the low value fresh SKUs (banana is on top of people’s minds) drive high conversion and bigger basket size hence it doesn’t necessarily reflect that. It is definitely a metric we want to start calculating and is included in scope of SC Project Proposal for Q3.

*Event Effective Date on or after* → Determine Value at Runtime → First day of next week

*Event Effective Date on or before* → Determine Value at Runtime → Last day of next week

Hi [~accountid:5bcf15233aa82432ce72a536], 

in this case, in accordance with Croatian legislation we have two options:

* terminate the agreement and claim for damages:
* ask decrease of the price and clam for damages. 

Since the landlord could argue that refurnishing the whole shopping center was necessary and he did not have any option, there is a possibility that the courts would allow the termination of the agreement. 

Therefore, if the alternative premises fit our needs, my opinion is that we should agree on it. However, you may ask and try to negotiate for an additional discount on the rent (due to the smaller surface and due to damage occurring without our fault) or you can ask for two months free. 

An alternative option is that we terminate the agreement and claim the damages, but most likely we would need to initiate the court proceeding in order to get the payment from the landlord. 

Should you have any questions, feel free to ask. 

Best regards, 

Iva

the tax counsels feedback as I sent you yesterday in the e-mail is the following:

_“We like to answer your below questions regarding German tax effects on handing out prizes to drivers in Germany as follows:_

# *_Assumptions for comments_*

* _Bolt OÜ has no German taxable presence (like permanent establishment)_
* _Bolt OÜ acts as intermediary/agent for ride hailing and has as such only direct relationships with fleet companies. Bolt itself is not rendering transportation services_
* _Commission for agent service is charged from Bolt OÜ to fleet companies either for all drivers together in a single invoice or via single invoices by Bolt OÜ to fleet company for each of its drivers_
* _Fleet companies’ drivers could be employees or self-employed, which provide the transportation service to the customer referred by Bolt OÜ through its App_
* _In no case is a driver employed by Bold OÜ_
* _Customer payment is routed from Bolt OÜ to fleet company after deducting Bolt’s agency fee_

 

* _Bolt OÜ intends to grant prizes to drivers and fleet companies for higher scope of provided rides and therefore higher agency fees for Bolt OÜ_
* _Prizes could be granted as (i) only one prize for best performer or (ii) prize for reaching certain margin_
* _Based on the contractual arrangements in place, neither the fleet companies nor the drivers have any right to claim the above prices from Bolt; the prices are a voluntary marketing expense by Bolt to promote good economic performance re Bolt’s ride hailing service_

 

# *_Income tax effects_*

_The granting of prizes has a direct temporal and economic connection with the performance of the fleet companies and their drivers. We therefore expect costs to be (tax) deductible at Bolt level (to be confirmed by local Estonian advisor). The prizes have therefore to be considered as taxable income for income tax/corporate income tax purposes at the level of the fleet company (granting of EUR 5,000 – EUR 10,000 to fleet company) respectively at the level of the individual driver (granting of eVouchers worth EUR 2,000 directly from Bolt OÜ to driver)._

 

_If the fleet company distributes the received prize to its drivers this has to be considered as operating expenses, ie income EUR 5,000 from receipt of prize and expenses of EUR 5,000 from transfer of prize to drivers resulting in profit of EUR 0. The drivers receive taxable employment income (wage tax obligation for fleet company in case of employees) or income from self employment (no wage tax obligation for fleet company). In case of employed drivers there should also be an impact on social security to be withheld by fleet company._

 

_There are no German withholding tax obligations for Bolt OÜ granting prizes to fleet company or drivers._

 

_Please note that the granting of prizes from Bolt OÜ directly to drivers who are employees of a fleet company results in a wage tax obligation for the fleet company according to sec. 38 para. 1 sentence 3 German Income Tax Act, if the fleet company knows or can recognize that such prize has been granted._

 

# *_VAT effects_*

_The final prizes are granted by means of monetary payments directly to the fleet companies. Bolt OÜ receives fees for its agency services rendered to the fleet companies. The final prizes qualify as a reduction of these fees received for the agency services, like the bonuses granted. As a consequence, Bolt OÜ should consider the final prizes in its EC Sales Lists (but this should be verified under Estonian VAT law) and the fleet companies in Germany should reduce the VAT liability under the reverse charge mechanism in Germany (section 13b German VAT Act). The final prizes are considered for VAT purposes when actually being paid._

 

_The weekly prizes are granted directly to the drivers by means of Amazon eVouchers. We understand that the Vouchers are not specified to certain products / suppliers. As the fleet companies are not involved in granting the weekly prizes, we are of the opinion that the weekly prizes do not effect the renumeration of the agency services rendered by Bolt OÜ to the fleet companies. But the weekly prizes are a renumeration for a service by the respective driver to Bolt OÜ. In case of a driver employed by a fleet company, we assume that the driver does not act as a taxable person (entrepreneur) that is there should be no VAT consequence. In case of a self-employed driver (being aware that the generally agency service is rendered by Bolt OÜ to the fleet company), we expect that Bolt OÜ needs to apply the reverse charge in Estonia (but this should be verified under Estonian VAT law), regardless whether the driver falls within the scope of the VAT simplification for SME or not._

_If you should have any further questions, please do not hesitate to contact us._

_Kind regards,”_

This fraud rule  (BUSINESS_COMPANY_HIGH_FRAUD_SCORE) triggers when the user is trying to create an order using a business payment method that belongs to a company with a negative balance. We allow businesses to make orders even if the payment fails, but the increase of the amount in each of these preparation attempts means the payment is failing and we keep adding it to their balance for the next order. And the company becomes high risk.

*What could be done?*

The admin of the company needs to clear the failed payments amount. In other words, the company must pay their debt, and once that is done, the users will be able to use the business payment method *within 24 to 48 hours after the payment is made.*

S’il s’agit d’approcher les chauffeurs aux abords des locaux de nos concurrents, alors cela peut s’envisager mais cela doit *rester sur le domaine publique* et *ne pas avoir lieu de manière régulière ni trop organisée*. Il ne faut pas abuser du *droit de libre concurrence* et il faut *respecter les règles d’un "commerce honnête"*.

+Quelques précisions+:

Le principe de liberté du commerce et de l’industrie a pour corollaire le principe de la libre concurrence. En vertu de ce principe, tout professionnel peut attirer à lui la clientèle de ses concurrents, sans que ceux-ci puissent lui reprocher.

Cependant, la liberté de la concurrence n’est pas absolue. *Elle ne permet pas aux entreprises d’user de procédés contraires aux usages loyaux du commerce pour nuire à un concurrent afin de détourner sa clientèle. Une action en concurrence déloyale peut alors être intentée.*

+Attention au démarchage déloyal de la clientèle:+
En principe, *il n’existe pas de droit privatif sur la clientèle. Ainsi, le simple démarchage de la clientèle d’un concurrent est licite dès lors qu’il n’est pas accompagné de procédés déloyaux* (Cass. Com. 24 octobre 2000), ou lorsque le déplacement de la clientèle procède d’initiatives spontanées de ladite clientèle (CA Versailles 11 septembre 1997) ou lorsque les contacts commerciaux résultent du libre jeu de la concurrence (CA Aix en Provence 4 mars 2003).

*Au contraire, constituent un acte de concurrence déloyale* : l'annonce mensongère à la clientèle du concurrent de la cessation des activités de celui-ci (CA Paris 21 octobre 1998) ; le fait de recourir à une publicité fausse ou de nature à induire en erreur (Cass. com., 9 févr. 1966) ; le fait de revendiquer de façon mensongère la totalité d'une installation ; ou encore *la prospection systématique des clients de l’entreprise concurrente* ; le fait de se recommander de la société concurrente (CA Paris, 27 mai 1992), etc.

+Attention aussi à “la confusion”.+ Une jurisprudence constante et abondante considère que le fait de créer, fût-ce par imprudence ou négligence, une confusion ou un risque de confusion avec l'entreprise d'un concurrent ou avec ses produits ou services constitue un acte de concurrence déloyale (CA Caen 4 février 2003). *« éviter tout risque de confusion »* Ainsi, les juges énoncent clairement qu’un « commerce honnête impose de dissiper la confusion qui peut naître dans l'esprit du public sur l'origine respective de deux produits similaires » (CA Paris, 24 mai 1960 ; CA Paris, 22 oct. 1987) et que « *la concurrence cesse d'être loyale… lorsqu'elle est faussée par des procédés ou des manoeuvres ayant pour objet d'entraîner une confusion dans l'esprit de la clientèle* » (CA Lyon, 23 janv. 1979).

+Enfin, attention au “dénigrement”+ - qui consiste à *jeter publiquement le discrédit sur les produits, l'entreprise ou la personnalité d'un concurrent dans le but de détourner sa clientèle ou plus généralement de lui nuire* dans un esprit de lucre (CA Lyon 21 mai 1974). Il faut que les concurrents dénigrés soient aisément identifiables (Cass. com., 9 juin 1980 ; CA Paris, 15 déc. 1994) et *le dénigrement est constitué même si les faits révélés par l'auteur du dénigrement sont exacts*. Le dénigrement peut être direct (informations malveillantes, critiques systématiques - CA Lyon, 21 mai 1974) ; viser les méthodes du concurrent pour fabriquer ou vendre ses produits (CA Paris, 15 juin 1981) ou la personne même du chef d'entreprise, sa compétence professionnelle ou son crédit (CA Paris, 7 mai 1982) ; ou indirect (attribuer à ses produits des qualités déniées aux produits ou entreprises.

*→* +Conclusion+*: La frontière entre comportement licite et illicite est souvent ténue - donc ne pas abuser de cette technique de démarchage, qui à mon sens doit rester ponctuelle et limitée* 😉

Dear \[DLA]

* We understand that there is in PT (i) a prohibition for platform operators to own or finance or be an interested party in the acquisition, renting or leasing of TVDE vehicles and (ii) a banking monopoly principle.
* Considering that the upfront payment would come from Bolt Operations OU, it seems that our best option would be to enter into *a co-investment contract with the FO* and to *include a settlement arrangement in both contracts* (in the co-investment contract with the FO and in the financing agreement between the Bank and the FO) - would you agree with that?
* I note that you also mentioned adopting a more general contractual object (for example, that the investment is aimed at a general corporate purpose). However we would *prefer to pay the bank directly*, if possible - or at least make it crystal clear that the funds should go towards buying the TVDE vehicles - so not sure how we can include a general contractual object in the contract…
* We would also *like the* +*co-investment contract*+ *to cover the following*:
** 2 years exclusivity for each car that we ‘co-finance’ → By that, we mean that we ask them that each car spends X online hours per week on the Bolt platform.
** KPIs for the FO: 
*** 1 global KPI: 45,000€ GMV minimum per car after 18 months after 1st ride of each car, which corresponds to the 2,250€ (5% of advanced cash-back) we are paying - we can include a 2 months grace period (so total 18+2) 
*** KPIs/metrics to be tracked weekly/monthly (e.g. Minimum Online Hours (i.e. hours connected with that car on the Bolt Platform), Minimum acceptance rate (how many rides they accept with the car), Minimum average trips per week, Minimum GMV per week/month
*** minimum 50 additional cars each (objective is 170 fo Apcar/ 150 for Wisentheimer).
*** we need to guarantee that XS will remain open for at least 4 years with mutual exclusivity in case utilisation lowers in other categories.
** Cash-back (on top of the initial upfront payment): If the FO exceeds the GMV target over 18 months, Bolt gives the FO a 5% Cash-back on the excess performance (= bonus paid by Bolt to the FO).

** Regular check points to verify that they’re meeting the KPIs/ are on track for targets.

{{Paho MQTT C}} is the most supported MQTT client that may hypothetically work on all mobile platforms of our interest or in the worst case scenario we could pair it with its sibling {{Paho MQTT Java}}, so this one was considered as the most promising dependency to consider. However after a few days of investigation and experiments it appeared that building a {{Paho MQTT C}} library for {{arm64}} and {{x86_64}} architecture using iOS toolchain is quite challenging and I still didn’t manage to make it work, so I decided to put this solution on hold and stick to a pair {{CocoaMQTT}} + {{HiveMQ MQTT}}. 

 {{CocoaMQTT}} can’t be added directly to a KMM module because of two open issue in KMM gradle plugin [KT-39122|https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-39122/CocoaPods-Gradle-plugin-doesnt-pass-fmodules-to-cinterop-tool-for-Swift-pods] and [KT-39120|https://youtrack.jetbrains.com/issue/KT-39120/Cinterop-tool-doesnt-support-the-fmodules-compiler-argument]. Another iOS [MQTT client|https://github.com/novastone-media/MQTT-Client-Framework] has a full different set of issues, but this library doesn’t seem to be supported by anyone, so it is better to stick to CocoaMQTT and wait when JetBrains fix their gradle plugin. So far we may use a workaround of adding {{CocoaMQTT}} dependency to {{chat-ios}} Swift module and provide an implementation to the cross-platform module from there.

In this regard there were created two modules {{chat-ios}} and {{chat-android}} that both will depend on a cross-platform {{chat-shared}} module. {{chat-shared}} module will provide an interface for {{MQTT}} client components that need to be created and platform specific {{chat-ios}} and {{chat-android}} will provide the implementations of these interfaces. All the logic should be places in {{chat-shared}} and platform specific modules must remain as thin as possible.

_Surname, first name?_
_E-mail address?_
_Phone number?_
_Do you need any help if finalizing your activation as a driver on our Platform?_
_Do you need any other help?_

* There should be a retention time set for this data that will be collected. Meaning that *after the surveys are conducted and drivers have been contacted/helped, the data should be deleted*. No fixed time limit, but +3 months+ would be good.

*15.1 contact person.* The _contracting parties_ designate a contractual-commercial and a technical contact person together with deputies with name, e-mail and telephone number for questions in connection with the implementation of this _contract_. The contact persons named by the _contractual partners_ at the time of the conclusion of this _contract_ and their deputies are named with their aforementioned contact details in *Annex 15.1* .of changes to the contact persons, their deputies or their contact details _contractual_ partners shall notify each other in writing (section 20.3) 

*15.2 IT security.* The _contractual_ partners will protect IT systems used for the cooperation against security risks and threats according to the generally recognized state of the art. If gaps or deficiencies are identified or suspected, the _contractual_ immediately adjust these protective measures accordingly. The _contractual partners_ will inform each other immediately about recognized or suspected security incidents and support them with reasonable economic effort in their defense and correction, if this is necessary.

h1. *16. Data protection and access to customer data Compliance*

*16.1 with data protection laws.* The _contractual partners_ undertake to comply with the provisions of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and Council of April 27, 2016 (“*GDPR*”) and the Federal Data Protection Act (“*BDSG*”) when processing personal data.

*16.2 Responsible body.* Subject to Clause 16.4, the _partner_ responsible for processing the personal data of the users that is collected via the _mobility apps_ and the _mobility platform_ for the purpose of booking the _mobility_ offer.

*16.3 order processing.* have regulated all existing duties and responsibilities on the subject of data protection _contractual_ to this _contract_ as *Annex 16.3* processing agreement attached

*16.4 Shared Accountability.* The partner processes personal data of the users for the purpose of booking the mobility offer in the mobility apps in joint responsibility with the B2B/B2G customers. The partner hereby commissions and authorizes Mobimeo to conclude the sample agreement on joint responsibility pursuant to Article 26 (1) sentence 2 GDPR attached to this contract as Annex 16.4 on behalf of the partner with each B2B/B2G customer whose mobility App the mobility offer is integrated. Deviations from the sample are only permitted after prior approval by the partner.

*19. Compliance*

*19.6 information security.* The contracting parties agree on the validity of the supplementary contract terms of Deutsche Bahn AG (DB AG) and its affiliated companies on information security requirements (EVB InformationsSicherheit), which are attached to this contract as Annex 19.6.

Useful query for getting the EC2 instance types where Savings Plan has applied:


{noformat}SELECT 
  bill_payer_account_id,
  line_item_usage_account_id,
  DATE_FORMAT((line_item_usage_start_date),'%Y-%m-%d') AS day_line_item_usage_start_date, 
  SPLIT_PART(savings_plan_savings_plan_a_r_n, '/', 2) AS savings_plan_savings_plan_a_r_n,
  savings_plan_offering_type,
  savings_plan_region,
  CASE 
  	WHEN line_item_product_code = 'AmazonECS' THEN 'Fargate'
  	WHEN line_item_product_code = 'AWSLambda' THEN 'Lambda'
  	ELSE product_instance_type_family 
  END AS case_instance_type_family,
  savings_plan_end_time,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(line_item_unblended_cost AS DECIMAL(16, 8))) AS sum_line_item_unblended_cost,
  SUM(TRY_CAST(savings_plan_savings_plan_effective_cost AS DECIMAL(16, 8))) AS sum_savings_plan_savings_plan_effective_cost
FROM 
  cost.cur_data
WHERE 
  year = '2022' and month = '6'
  AND savings_plan_savings_plan_a_r_n <> ''
  AND line_item_line_item_type = 'SavingsPlanCoveredUsage'
GROUP BY 
  bill_payer_account_id,
  line_item_usage_account_id,
  DATE_FORMAT((line_item_usage_start_date),'%Y-%m-%d'),
  SPLIT_PART(savings_plan_savings_plan_a_r_n, '/', 2),
  savings_plan_offering_type,
  savings_plan_region,
  7, -- refers to case_instance_type_family
  savings_plan_end_time
ORDER BY 
  day_line_item_usage_start_date;
{noformat}

Please note that we may forward your personal data inserted into this form to \[name/category of the partner] who may contact you with their \[car lease/rental] offer. I just found out from my Privacy colleagues that if we’re looking into paying for using someone’s image, then no GDPR-related wording will be required in the agreement itself, as the processing will be carried out on the basis of contractual necessity.
Otherwise, *for non-paid partnerships, as someone’s image is classified as personal data, the processing is usually based on data subject’s consent which unfortunately means that it can be revoked at any time*. So bottom line, if we don't pay the person and we say it's a consent to use her image rights for X years, this may be not enforceable as under GDPR the consent can be withdrawn at any time.

*→ If we want to secure the right to use it for 3 years, we would need to include some benefit that can be provided by Bolt to make it more of a contract*. Then we can process their image based on contractual necessity and the data subject won’t be able to withdraw their consent.

*FD Regional Support Team*


+_Kick-off meeting - 27 June ‘22_+



*Participants*  

Nigel Janssen & Irena Štefančić

*Project background*  

Regional Leads (RL) in food delivery operate in clear and open transparency. Now that we have a new RL starting in July ‘22, Masego suggested having a group sync instead of individual conversations about the same topic. 

This would save us meeting time between CS L&Ds and RLs be able to share news, updates, concerns, etc. and decide on correct action steps needed and create timelines and set clear expectations/responsibilities. 


*Goals and Scope*

_Regional MKA outliers_

* Briefly describe the issue - positive and negative outliers e.g repeat offenders (agents and markets)
* Share MKA findings narrative 
* In some cases, share targeted metric for the MKA
* Decide on the next steps/actions and set a timeline (document)



_Major news from each region_ 

* Market launches and updates (both from L&D and RLs) For example, global MKAs, different points of contact, news from Suppliers, etc.
* Share news or updates with relevant team/stakeholders. 




_Region’s TLs’ knowledge gaps and learning needs_ 

* Decide how and who will communicate this
* Understand the reason or root cause
* Provide suggested learning courses or assess what needs to be created
* The process to follow would be: RL/STL/TL should send an SD ticket and L&D assesses through a training needs analysis.


_Region’s IN and OS knowledge gaps_

* This can come from the L&D team or from RLs. 
* Present the issue/find the root cause and then formulate a solution (does not necessarily have to mean a training course is required - for example, Kb updates)
* For OS, gather feedback, request examples, deep dives, results, etc. L&D to review and consult with either responsible L&D for the said supplier or consult directly with the supplier. Once reviewed, request feedback/results and share with RLs in follow-up sync.
* RLs are welcome to bring an STL to the call to elaborate on the issue if needed. 




_Engagement in the region_

* Share information on current and/or upcoming talent development programs, courses, etc and collecting feedback support is needed.
* L&D to check in with those L&Ds responsible for these programs. 
* RLs to share and promote programs with STLs.



_Region’s health metrics (KPIs)_

* Identify pain points for the region - this can be shared by either party. If a project is in the pipeline, assess the goal and desired outcome/s. Should support be required from the KM team, check with the team for those available to collaborate on the project. A clear project plan would need to be created. 


_STLs’ and RL’s learning needs_  

* Collect feedback about potential training needs.
* This would be specific to these groups (if not LOB specific, notify Region support L&Ds).



_Potential quarterly projects for the region_ 

* Discuss any potential/planned projects for a region. Introduce projects for the quarter from our side and offer Local Trainer Bootcamps, so that agents can collaborate with L&D (ties in with the Badger Wheel).



*Additional Points:*

_Communication structure_

* Monthly call sync with Irena, Nigel, Masego and Joshua 
* Slack group chat for follow-up or urgent matters
* Confluence page - track action steps - mark progress



_Meeting notes/action steps_

* Confluence page to be created - possibly use STL space or decide on another
* Meeting notes to be added to the page for monitoring action steps (agendas could also be added).

{code:sql}with tasks_launch_in_city as (
select 
	c.name as city_name, 
	min(date_trunc('week',resolved_at)) first_task_closed_week
from rental.rental_order_vehicle_task rovt 
join admin_system_city c on rovt.city_id = c.id
where state='closed'
group by 1
)
select 
	sum(case when week_from_the_start in (-4,-3,-2,-1) then working_time else null end) working_time_before,
	sum(case when week_from_the_start in (-4,-3,-2,-1) then ops else null end) ops_before,
	sum(case when week_from_the_start in (1,2,3,4) then working_time else null end) working_time_after,
	sum(case when week_from_the_start in (1,2,3,4) then ops else null end) ops_after
from (
select city_name,
--date_trunc('week',created) ts_week,
week_from_the_start,
count(*) ops,
sum(case when till_next_action < 3*60 then till_next_action else null end) working_time--,
--1.0*ops/working_time*60
from 
(
select t.*,
tlc.first_task_closed_week,
date_diff('minute',lag(created,1) over (partition by external_id order by created asc), created) AS till_next_action,
date_diff('week',first_task_closed_week, date_trunc('week',created)) AS week_from_the_start
from
(
select
  ct.id as city_id,
  ct.name as city_name,
  ce.created,
  ce.to_state,
  c.external_type,
  c.external_id,
  ce.connection_id,
  c.search_category_id,
  c.vehicle_id
from rental.rental_order_charger_action_collect_event ce
join rental.rental_order_charger_action_collect c on ce.charger_action_collect_id=c.id and ce.connection_id = c.connection_id
join rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc on c.search_category_id=sc.id
join admin_system_city ct on sc.city_id=ct.id
where ce.created>date'2022-04-01'
and ce.to_state = 'collected'
union all
select
  ct.id as city_id,
  ct.name as city_name,
  ce.created,
  ce.to_state,
  c.external_type,
  c.external_id,
  ce.connection_id,
  c.search_category_id,
  c.vehicle_id
from rental.rental_order_charger_action_change_battery_event ce
join rental.rental_order_charger_action_change_battery c on ce.charger_action_change_battery_id=c.id and ce.connection_id = c.connection_id
join rental.rental_fleet_search_category sc on c.search_category_id=sc.id
join admin_system_city ct on sc.city_id=ct.id
where ce.created>date'2022-04-01'
and ce.to_state = 'battery_changed'
) t 
join tasks_launch_in_city tlc on t.city_name=tlc.city_name
where external_type ='charger'
order by external_id asc, created asc
)
group by 1,2
order by 1 asc, 2 asc
)
{code}

Hi all,

As you will have read in the email from the external counsel, she does not consider that there is a business succession and, therefore, an obligation on Bolt to employ the Novo Rehum workers. 

Please see below the advice we have received from the external counsel and attached the email chain:

*_Bolt legal: Whether or not articles 44 of the Workers' Statute and 130.2 of the Public Sector Contracts Law apply in this instance and if there is a business succession in this case and therefore if Bolt is obliged to employ the workers of Novo Rehum S.L.U.?_*

_External counsel: We understand that there is no obligation to subrogate the employees of Novo Rehum for the following reasons:_

_(i) There is no transfer of undertaking ("sucesión de empresa") of a business unit that determines the application of article 44 of WS (transposing EU TUPE regulations), given that there is only a mere change of holder of the authorization to operate e-scooters in Zaragoza, without any type of transfer of material or immaterial elements between the outgoing company and the incoming company; Such transfer of assets being an essential element in order to trigger the application of TUPE regulations in Spain._

 _(ii) According to your e-mail, the tender conditions do not include the obligation to subrogate those employees, and we understand that the CBA applicable to Bolt does not contain such an obligation either._

_(iii) The burofax is mainly supported in article 130.2 of Law 9/2017, dated 8 November, on public procurement law, which sets forth that "When the company that has been carrying out the service that is the object of the contract to be awarded is a Special Employment Centre, the company that is awarded the contract will have the obligation to subrogate itself as the employer of all the people with disabilities that have been carrying out their activity in the execution of the aforementioned contract"._

_However, our opinion is that article 130.2 of Law 9/2017 is not applicable in this case. There are various reasons:_

_(i) Article 9 of Law 9/2017 expressly excludes its application to concessions and authorisations on assets in the public domain and contracts for the exploitation of assets. This means that the authorisation to use the public domain is not regulated by Law 9/2017, and therefore none of the provisions included in Law 9/2017 are applicable, except in those cases where the terms and conditions specifically refers to such Law._

_(ii) Although we have not had access to the terms and conditions regulating the previous authorisation to use the public domain for the operation of the e-scooters in Zaragoza awarded to Novo Rehum S.L.U (the "previous terms") the terms and conditions regulating the authorisation awarded to Bolt (the "new terms"), which should be very similar to the previous terms, do not include Law 9/2017 as an applicable law to the authorisation. The only references in the new terms to the application of Law 9/2017 are in clause 2 (which states the applicable legal framework) establishing that such law is only applicable to procedural matters, when such reference is expressly made in the terms and conditions. The only references we have found in the new terms are in fact referred to procedural aspects._

 *_Bolt legal: How Bolt should proceed?_*

_External counsel: Consequently, our recommendation would be to reply briefly to the burofax received, denying the subrogation obligation, without giving much more explanation than the above._

_If the Novo Rehum S.L.U   does not take charge of these employees, they will most likely file a claim for dismissal, both to Novo Rehum S.L.U, and Bolt and Reby Rides S.L. before Labour Courts._

_Labour Courts will decide whether, (i) as we believe, there was no obligation of subrogation, and Novo Rehum is the exclusively responsible for the consequences of the dismissal of the employees, or (ii) whether, on the contrary, there was a legal obligation of subrogation, and Bolt and/or Reby Rides must assume the responsibility for the consequences of the dismissal of the employees (payment of 33 days of salaries per year worked)._  

----

Once drafted, I will send it to you so [~accountid:5bf7a8fb7ffaec527a023256] can sign it on behalf of Boltest and send it to Novo Rehum S.L.U. via burofax.

After spending some more time on investigation of this issue here is what was found out:

* The issue is not reproducing on {{debug}} builds where code obfuscation/optimisation is disabled (this was quite obvious because without code optimisation nothing can remove the code from a compiled binary).
* The issue is not reproducing on {{release}} build where code obfuscation/optimisation is enabled. This was checked multiple times by me and by [~accountid:5f83f9ff0c961300698c7094] with builds assembled locally and on CI.
* We do not have reports for the last 90 in Crashlytics having {{MqttChannelInitializer}}, {{MqttSslInitializer}} or {{NoSuchMethodError}}. Besides we haven’t noticed any issues with chat in production on our backend recently, while this issue is reproducing at least on {{DA.37.0}} which is in production for quite a while.
* The issue is reproducing only on {{smokeTest}} build type which is used by QA team to perform tests before release. This build is a mix of {{debug}} and {{release}} type in a sense that it has logs enabled as in {{debug}} but it also has obfuscation/optimisation enabled as well as in {{release}}. 
* With {{smokeTest}} build the issue is always reproducible on any Android phone. It is not device specific, but rather a “build type“ specific bug.

These findings give us a confirmation that the issue does not affect our users in production, but affects only our QA team which is also a bad thing as we may miss some issues in chat if the QA can’t properly test them. Though it is not that critical as it seemed in the beginning.

----

The main reason why MQTT broker can not be connected on {{smokeTest}} builds is because this build type has synthetic lambda java classes removed by R8 (Android tool for code obfuscation and optimisation) for some reason as it considers these classes as unused, while they are actually used. Besides R8 doesn’t remove these classes from {{release}} builds (or it does, but it also removes some other code that calls the missing lambda expression). The missing class belongs to a 3d party dependency (MQTT Client) that we use in chat and this class is only accessed internally by this library. Experimenting with R8 options to exclude certain classes that belongs to this library from optimising them didn't take any effect as excluding one class it shows that some other parts of the library are missing anyway (eg. some variables or functions that belong to other classes). Our chat library is configured according to [recommendations|https://hivemq.github.io/hivemq-mqtt-client/docs/installation/android/] of the developer who maintains this MQTT Client library and contains the following exclude rules are added in our configuration two years ago:

{noformat}-keepclassmembernames class io.netty.** { *; }
-keepclassmembers class org.jctools.** { *; }{noformat}

So the fact that the library is configured correctly and it works fine in {{release}} build gives us understanding that the issue is in {{smokeTest}} build configuration and the way how R8 works in this configuration. The fact that this configuration affects chat is a pure “luck” because the same could have happened to any other 3d party dependency or even our own code. 

Since we in Comms do not have a full understanding of how build environment in Driver App is configured and what are the reasons of enabling code optimisation to debug builds we can not provide a solution to fix this issue. Because Driver Android team understands the build configuration of their app better we would recommend them to take care of this issue taking all the information above as a starting point. 

The only recommendation we can give so far is to upgrade {{Android Gradle Plugin}} in Driver App project to the most recent version (at the moment it’s {{7.2.1}}) as there were made some changes in R8 that potentially could fix the current issue. Besides they added something that is called [precise shrinking|https://developer.android.com/studio/releases/gradle-plugin#experimental_further_app_size_reductions] which also could help.

MQTT features used in Bolt Rider and Driver clients for iOS and Android

*MQTT protocol Version*: 3.1.1
*Transport*: WebSocket
*QoS* for publishing and subscribing: (1) At Least Once (iOS subscribes with QoS 2, but this should be changed either in Tier 0 or Tier 1)
*API type*: Asynchronous

Used APIs

* Connecting to a broker via provided credentials (asynchronously return connection status)
** Clean Session: false _On Android there used TRUE, but this should be changed if possible._
** Transport: WebSocket (address: mqtt, query: version, device_id, device_name, device_type, language, session_id, mqtt_client_id, country)
** Connection parameters: Broker ID, Host, Port, Use SSL = TRUE, 
** Credentials: Rider = phone number/authUuid, Driver = empty string/accessToken
** Keep Alive: 10s _On iOS keep alive is turned off, but it should be set if possible._
* Disconnecting from a broker
* Subscribing to a topic (asynchronously return subscription status). A topic is never unsubscribed, but just disconnecting from a broker
** QoS 1 (at least once) _On iOS there is used 2 (exactly once), but this should be changed to 1 if possible._
** Topic Name: Rider = sub/\{user_id}, Driver = sub/\{driver_id}
** Payload: json
* Publishing messages to a topic
** QoS 1 (at least once)
** Topic Name: Rider = pub/\{user_id}, Driver = pub/\{driver_id}
** Payload: json

In iOS we need to provide a replacement for {{MQTTSession}} and in Android - for {{Mqtt3Client}}.

Hi Marja-Liisa,

Below I’ll take you through an example of a use case. 

*Step 1: We acquire affiliates.* The traditional concept of affiliates is mostly online but we will widen the audience. Our first and best affiliates would be companies/people in constant communication with drivers e.g car rental companies, garage, gas stations, car wash companies, fingerprint check hubs, etc. From an online perspective, we can also onboard brand ambassadors and influencers. But anyone who knows people who can become Bolt drivers can be an affiliate, we can also reach out to them on social medial by throwing an ad to recruit affiliates.

*Step 2: Onboard affiliates*. If we have already details of the affiliates, we send them directly an email with a link to sign up within the Awin platform. If we don’t have their details for example in a recruitment ad, they can sign up directly on the platform. After putting their personal information, at the end of the process, they will need to accept the Bolt (which we are writing here) and [+Awin+|https://www.awin.com/gb/publisher-terms] T&Cs. Note that after signing up, Bolt has the right to accept or reject their application.

*Step 3: The affiliates reach out to their contacts.* On the Awin platform, the affiliates will have access to their personalised link (i.e a link to the Driver portal landing page that has a specific tracking feature that links a sign up to the relevant affiliate) or a personal referral code. The affiliate will then use one or all to share with their contacts/network outside of the Awin platform. We can also make some visuals and banners available for them to use on their social media if they are online.

*Step 4: The interested drivers sign up.* The drivers sign up directly on our landing page either by using the affiliates link or inputting the referral code in Step 2 of the reg form. This is where things could become confusing:
(1) if the driver opts out of tracking cookies on their browser, they won’t be traceable and therefore the affiliate won’t be able to claim their commission
(2) if the driver inputs incorrectly the referral code or forget to input it, it’s hard to argue whether this sign up came from the affiliates - maybe the suggestion is that we don’t pay if the referral code is not clearly inputted? 

*Step 5: The affiliates get their commissions*. We set the commission structure and rule directly on the Awin platform which the affiliate sees when generating their links. We can also define multiple commission structures and assign them individually to certain affiliate specifically. The commission structure also includes the success criteria (for example say they get €50 after the driver’s 1st trip). Bolt will be reviewing weekly (not confirmed) all the conversions by affiliate and will be approving and rejecting whether we will be paying for the conversion (to avoid fraud).
Note that in the current set up, the affiliate should receive their payment every month (tbc when exactly), paid by Awin, and only after Bolt has paid everything to Awin so Awin doesn’t get in a position of credit holder.


The only thing the affiliate is obliged to do is to not bring bad publicity and build a negative reputation around Bolt. We can also request that any post on social media needs to have our review and approval. They also must delete anything we ask them to.

I think it’s also worth highlighting that we will not compensate for drivers with existing accounts.


I think this is but I will continue to think about other points. The Brand Ambassador T&C already gathers a lot of point. Let me know if you have any more questions or would like to have any more info.

Kind regards,
Karina

Αρ. φακ.: 5.10.5.3

 

Κύριοι,

 

Έχω οδηγίες να αναφερθώ στο πιο πάνω θέμα και σε συνέχεια του ηλεκτρονικού μου μηνύματος με  ημερ. 17.6.2022 σας ενημερώνω προκαταρτικά για βασικές πρόνοιες της περί Ασφάλειας και Υγείας στην Εργασία Νομοθεσίας ως ακολούθως:

 

# Σύμφωνα με τους Κανονισμούς 4(1) και (2) των περί Διαχείρισης Θεμάτων Ασφάλειας και Υγείας στην Εργασία Κανονισμών του 2021 (Κ.Δ.Π. 158/2021) πρέπει να υπάρχει διαθέσιμη γραπτή εκτίμηση των υφιστάμενων κατά την εργασία κινδύνων που δημιουργούνται από τις διεργασίες και άλλες δραστηριότητες του υποστατικού / επιχείρησής σας με βάσει την οποία να καθορίζονται τα προληπτικά και προστατευτικά μέτρα που πρέπει να λαμβάνονται για την προστασία εργοδοτουμένων ή και άλλων προσώπων στην εργασία.

 

Πρέπει να καθορίζονται με βάση τη γραπτή εκτίμηση για όλους τους κινδύνους από όλες τις δραστηριότητές σας, τα απαιτούμενα προληπτικά και προστατευτικά μέτρα ανά θέση εργασίας και ανά δραστηριότητα. Στη γραπτή εκτίμηση κινδύνων (ΓΕΚ) πρέπει να περιλαμβάνονται οι πηγές κινδύνου, τα πρόσωπα που επηρεάζονται, τα μέτρα που ήδη έχουν ληφθεί και τα πρόσθετα μέτρα (οργανωτικά και τεχνικά) που πρέπει να ληφθούν, καθώς και τα πρόσωπα που είναι υπεύθυνα για την εφαρμογή των μέτρων αυτών. Στα μέτρα αυτά πρέπει να περιλαμβάνονται, μεταξύ άλλων, η παροχή εκπαίδευσης, η εγκατάσταση εξοπλισμού, οι μέθοδοι εργασίας, καθώς και το υλικό ή ο εξοπλισμός προστασίας που πρέπει να χρησιμοποιηθεί. Η εφαρμογή των μέτρων πρέπει να διασφαλίζεται μέσω διαδικασιών ή/και σχεδίου δράσης που καθορίζεται στο σύστημα διαχείρισης των κινδύνων.

 

# Σύμφωνα με τον Κανονισμό 5 των εν λόγω Κανονισμών πρέπει να  εφαρμόζεται κατάλληλο και επαρκές Σύστημα Διαχείρισης των Κινδύνων που διατρέχουν εργοδοτούμενα πρόσωπα ή και άλλα πρόσωπα που δεν εργοδοτούνται, αλλά πιθανόν να επηρεάζονται από τις δραστηριότητές σας.  Το Σύστημα αυτό πρέπει να περιλαμβάνει, μεταξύ άλλων (α) την πολιτική για τα θέματα ασφάλειας και υγείας, καθώς και τις διευθετήσεις για την κατάλληλη εφαρμογή και κοινοποίηση της σε όλους τους εργοδοτούμενους (β) τις διευθετήσεις για την οργάνωση, τον αποτελεσματικό προγραμματισμό υλοποίησης, την εφαρμογή, τον έλεγχο, την παρακολούθηση και την αναθεώρηση των προληπτικών και προστατευτικών μέτρων που καθορίζονται με βάση τη ΓΕΚ, (γ) τα ονόματα και τα καθήκοντα των εργοδοτουμένων που ορίζονται για να διεκπεραιώνουν τις διαδικασίες παρακολούθησης των μέτρων, (δ) τα στοιχεία της εκπαίδευσης των εργαζομένων σε θέματα ασφάλειας και υγείας, (ε) τις διευθετήσεις για τον χειρισμό εκτάκτων περιστατικών, (στ) τις διευθετήσεις για την τήρηση αρχείων που προβλέπονται από τη νομοθεσία για ασφάλεια και υγεία στην εργασία και (ζ) όπου εφαρμόζεται, τις διευθετήσεις για την εκπόνηση και εφαρμογή του Σχεδίου Ασφάλειας και Υγείας. Πρέπει, να τηρείται όλα τα αναγκαία έγγραφα και αποδεικτικά στοιχεία που να τεκμηριώνουν ότι εφαρμόζεται το Σύστημα αυτό.

·         Βεβαιώνεστε ότι ο άλλος εργοδότης ή αυτοεργοδοτούμενο  πρόσωπο διαθέτει επαρκείς γνώσεις και την πείρα καθώς και τα αναγκαία έγγραφα άδειες και πιστοποιητικά για τη διεξαγωγή της εργασίας.

 

# Ιδιαίτερα σε σχέση με τους διανομείς έτοιμων φαγητών, ακόμα και εάν αυτοί δεν εργοδοτούνται από εσάς,  εξακολουθείτε να έχετε υποχρέωση για συμμόρφωση με όσα αναφέρονται πιο πάνω, δηλ. αυτοί πρέπει να περιλαμβάνονται στην ΓΕΚ και το Σύστημα Διαχείρισης των Κινδύνων που εφαρμόζετε και να διαθέτετε / παρουσιάζετε έγγραφα / στοιχεία / τεκμήρια που να αποδεικνύουν τη συμμόρφωσή σας με τα πιο πάνω όπως για παράδειγμα:

·         κριτήρια επιλογής των συνεργατών σας για τέτοιου είδους εργασίες,

·         καθορισμό ελάχιστων υποχρεώσεων με τις οποίες οι συνεργάτες σας οφείλουν να συμμορφώνονται για ομαλή συνεργασία,

·         διαθεσιμότητα διαδικασιών όπως π.χ. για διαχείριση παραπόνων, ατυχήματος / έκτακτης ανάγκης, καταγγελιών, μη συμμορφώσεων

·         καλλιέργεια / προώθηση κουλτούρας ασφάλειας και υγείας

 

# Περαιτέρω και επειδή το ΤΕΕ, προτίθεται στο πλαίσιο της ετήσιας εκστρατείας 

+Επιθεώρησης Ξενοδοχείων, Εστιατορίων και Υποστατικών Διανομής Έτοιμων Φαγητών+ κατά το μήνα Σεπτέμβριο του 2022 να διενεργήσει επιθεωρήσεις σε υποστατικά διανομής έτοιμων φαγητών παρακαλώ όπως γνωστοποιήσετε στο ΤΕΕ τα στοιχεία επικοινωνίας (όνομα / διεύθυνση / τηλέφωνο) των νομικών προσώπων με τα οποία συνεργάζεστε για την ένταξη διανομέων έτοιμων φαγητών στο δίκτυό σας ώστε να διευθετηθούν οι εν λόγω επιθεωρήσεις στα υποστατικά τους.  Για καθορισμό των προτεραιοτήτων της εκστρατείας η συμπερίληψη στον εν λόγω κατάλογο του αριθμού των διανομέων έτοιμων φαγητών από κάθε νομικό πρόσωπο θα ήταν υποβοηθητική.  Σε περίπτωση που αυτό δεν είναι δυνατό παρακαλώ καταχωρίστε τα νομικά πρόσωπα ανά δυναμικότητα αρχίζοντας από αυτά που εργοδοτούν τους περισσότερους διανομείς έτοιμων φαγητών.  Επί τους παρόντος παρακαλώ όπως οι αυτοεργοδοτούμενοι εξαιρεθούν από τον πιο πάνω κατάλογο.  Επίσης, επειδή το ΤΕΕ βρίσκεται στη διαδικασία ετοιμασίας σχετικού προγράμματος επιθεωρήσεων, παρακαλώ όπως ο σχετικός κατάλογος αποσταλεί εάν είναι δυνατό μέχρι τη Δευτέρα 4.7.2022.
